task: Review this fictional healthcare-technology marketing claim. Marketing is the primary genre; apply medical safeguards to the health-outcome reference. Identify the unsupported efficacy claim and explain what evidence is needed before it can be used.
input: ClinicFlow has been clinically proven to reduce missed appointments and improve patient health outcomes in primary care settings.

facts.text: ClinicFlow is a fictional patient-scheduling software.
The supplied facts contain no clinical trial or peer-reviewed study supporting the efficacy claim.
No regulatory clearance or health-outcome data is included in the supplied facts.

forbidden_additions: A general claim that scheduling tools typically improve health outcomes.
preserve: The identification of both missing evidence types: appointment data and a health-outcome study.
The marketing scope without substituting a patient-information format.
The medical-safeguard application to the health-outcome claim specifically.
